title: An-Nas: the people
hook: refuge with the Lord of people from the whisperer who withdraws (Surah 114)

segments.voice: Yesterday: the ta'awwudh, seeking refuge before reciting. Your line was refuge, then the name. Did you set one distraction down before you began something? Day one hundred fifty-nine.

It's two in the morning. The house is quiet, and a voice in your head is not. You're not good enough. They were laughing at you. Check your phone one more time. It doesn't shout. It whispers, and it's very patient. The Qur'an ends, its very last surah, number one hundred fourteen, with exactly this voice. Six short lines, and a picture of the whisperer that surprises people: it sneaks in, and it slips away. Today we start reading the last part of the Qur'an, from its final page backward. Today: An-Nas, the people.
screen: `2AM, AND A VOICE THAT WHISPERS.` → `THE LAST SURAH OF THE QUR'AN.` → `READING FROM THE END.`

segments.voice: Here is how Pickthall translates the opening: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, The King of mankind, The God of mankind. Notice the word mankind three times. In Arabic it's an-nas, the people, and every line of the surah ends on that same sound: nas, nas, nas, and then khannas, and nas again. Read aloud, it rocks like a lullaby, and that may be on purpose. Allah is named three ways here: Lord, the one who raises and cares for you; King, the one in charge; God, the one who is worshipped. Three doors to the same refuge. And the danger is named once, in two words: al-waswas al-khannas. Waswas is the whisper, a word that sounds like what it means. Khannas means the one who draws back, who shrinks away and hides. Commentators explain the picture: the whisperer comes when you forget Allah, and retreats when you remember Him. The whisper can't hold its ground against remembrance. It only works while it's unnoticed. The surah ends by saying the whisperers come from among the jinn and from among people. Some of the voices that pull you down are unseen. Some have phone numbers. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ loved these last surahs. Aisha reports in Bukhari that every night before sleep he would cup his hands, recite al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas into them, and wipe his hands over his body, three times. So the last page of the book is also, for many Muslims, the last thing said before the lights go out.
screen: `LORD, KING, GOD — THREE DOORS.` · `WASWAS — THE WHISPER.` · `KHANNAS — THE ONE WHO DRAWS BACK.` · `THE LAST WORDS BEFORE SLEEP.` · then, large: `THE WHISPERER WITHDRAWS.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice for tonight, but start it now. Sit, and let one recent whisper come to mind, the kind that sounds like your own voice but isn't kind. Don't argue with it. Just notice it and name it: that's a whisper. If you pray, you can say the first line of the surah, qul a'udhu bi rabbin-nas, and let it be the remembering. Then watch what the whisper does when it's looked at directly. Tonight, before sleep, you can come back here. The bell holds the time.
An-Nas. The people, the name of the Qur'an's last surah: refuge in the Lord of people from the whisperer who draws back. Today's word.
Your line: the whisperer withdraws. When a mean voice starts up in your head today, name it as a whisper, and remember something true instead. See whether it backs off. Day one hundred fifty-nine.

howItsDone: Many Muslims recite Surah an-Nas with al-Falaq and al-Ikhlas before sleep, blowing lightly into cupped hands and wiping them over the body, following the Prophet's practice; it is also recited after the prayers and for protection.

fork.setup: it's night, and the Prophet is going to sleep. what does Aisha say he did first?
options: recited the last three surahs into cupped hands and wiped his body
sat silent until he fell asleep
fork.reveal: he recited al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas into his hands and wiped them over his body, three times (Bukhari). the book's last page became his last words of the day.

original.note: Arabic: the people, mankind. every line of Surah 114 ends on this sound.

trapdoor: what you thought: a short surah about people.
what it means: refuge in the Lord, King and God of people from the whisperer who sneaks in and draws back.
what a scholar hears: al-waswas al-khannas; commentators say it retreats at the remembrance of Allah; 114:6 names whisperers from the jinn and from mankind.
